eligibility: At least two actual people outside the project team. AI agents, developers reviewing their own work, browser tests, and simulated personas do not count.
reasonNotRun: The lead explicitly moved these sessions to future usability research on 2026-11-03. No participants have been recruited or observed; no consent, feedback or results are invented.

protocol.purpose: Evaluate whether outside people can understand and recover through the target student-aid evidence journey, including the meaning of uncertainty and encryption boundaries.
preparation: Open prototype.html directly in a browser; use only embedded fictional records.
Explain the design badge, navigation, scenario buttons, and that nothing is created, uploaded, saved, exported, synced, or deleted.
Use participant codes P01 and P02 instead of names, email addresses, school identifiers, account numbers, or other personal data.
Ask for explicit consent before timing or taking non-sensitive notes; do not record audio, video, or screen unless a separate explicit consent is documented.
Start each task from its catalog start screen using the target journey navigation or screen selector.
Reset the prototype between participants. Do not demonstrate a task solution before the participant attempts it.
protocol.consentScript: This is a fictional design prototype. We want to learn where the screens are unclear. Please do not use real records, credentials, recovery secrets, or personal details. Participation is voluntary; you may skip any task or stop. With your permission, I will record task outcomes and non-sensitive usability notes under an anonymous code. No recording is needed. May I proceed?
moderatorScript: Ask the task prompt verbatim and invite the participant to think aloud.
Observe the first attempt before giving help. Ask neutral follow-ups such as "What would you expect here?" and "What tells you that?".
Record completion as unassisted, assisted, failed, or skipped; record prompts and elapsed seconds.
If the participant tries to enter real information, stop that entry and return to synthetic examples.
After each task ask what felt unclear and ask for confidence from 1 (uncertain) to 5 (certain).
At the end ask which screen or term they would change first. Do not ask for sensitive student-aid stories.

severityVocabulary.critical: Could lead to false approval, false entitlement/match, secret disclosure, irreversible-loss misunderstanding, or false deletion/backup success.
severityVocabulary.major: Cannot complete a core task or recover without a moderator hint.
severityVocabulary.minor: Hesitation, navigation friction, or language issue without a trust-boundary mistake.

successCriteria: Both sessions belong to distinct outside humans with consent and actual start/end timestamps.
Every task has an observed outcome, help count, non-sensitive notes, and criterion results; skipped tasks remain visibly skipped.
Both people can distinguish proposals from approved facts, source-backed explanation from entitlement, and unknown evidence from zero.
Both people can distinguish login from decryption recovery, device-copy deletion from single synced-case deletion and whole-account purge, and pending sync/deletion from completion.
Any critical or major issue becomes an explicit design change and retest requirement; local automated tests do not waive it.
protocol.completionRule: Keep status not-run and sessions empty until actual consented sessions occur. Future research completion requires two real outside-human sessions and documented observations/fixes/retests. The lead deferred this research; it no longer blocks foundation issue #34 under decision D11.

tasks.prompt: You want to inspect a fictional aid trail while keeping control of who can read it. Start a case, compare a local-only choice with an optional sync account, then explain what you would do after losing access to a device.
scenarios: Successful account login but locked case
successCriteria: Find local-only setup without being forced to create an account.
Explain that login-password reset does not recover encryption keys.
Find a safe exit after wrong recovery material and recognize when a case cannot be recovered.
Explain that logout does not delete a case or account.
observe: First choice and reason
Any real-credential entry attempt (stop it immediately)
Confusion between account login, local unlock, and recovery
Whether failure remains recoverable without moderator instruction

tasks.prompt: The fictional bank CSV has a date, amount, and memo. Prepare a preview, then try a source layout that the app cannot read and an empty CSV. Find a way to continue with a manual observation.
successCriteria: Identify the date, amount, sign rule, and event role before proceeding.
Recognize that unsupported, invalid, and empty input has created no approved fact.
Find manual fallback and identify its provenance as manual.
observe: Whether sample controls are mistaken for actual file uploads
Mapping choices and corrected errors
Whether an empty file is interpreted as zero
Recovery path chosen for unsupported format

tasks.prompt: Two proposed credits look alike and another row is unsupported. Decide what can be approved. Then imagine the case changed on another device just before approval.
successCriteria: Use source identity and row content rather than equal dollar amounts alone to discuss duplication.
Keep repeated/deferred and unsupported rows unapproved.
Check the review acknowledgement before simulated approval.
Return to review after a stale revision and do not claim the failed action saved a fact.
observe: Reason for duplicate decision
Understanding of proposal versus fact
Whether participant notices unchecked review gate
Response to stale approval

tasks.prompt: Explain to a friend why the fictional school surplus changed, and show the records that support your explanation. Now the original bill is missing on this device; investigate both a matching and a different replacement.
successCriteria: Explain $1,500 to $900 as a $300 grant correction plus a $300 school charge.
Find source positions and approval/correction records.
State that equal $900 refund and bank amounts do not confirm a match.
Recognize a mismatched file does not replace the old source and find the retry path.
observe: Amounts and source references participant uses
Entitlement or document-authenticity assumptions
Whether unavailable source bytes are visible
Response to mismatch and safe exit

tasks.prompt: A corrected fictional statement reduces a school charge from $300 to $250. Review the effect and explain what happens to the earlier record. Then identify something the case still cannot tell you.
successCriteria: Predict and confirm a $50 increase in school surplus from $900 to $950.
Find both original $300 approval and $250 correction history.
Identify at least one unknown source/date range without inventing zero or a fee.
Find a way to add evidence or keep the unknown visible.
observe: Prediction before confirmation
Whether old source is assumed to be overwritten
Understanding of the separate correction branch
Any assumption that provided records establish full coverage

tasks.prompt: You are offline after local work, and later another device has changed the same case. Find out what is safe to say about backup status and review the competing versions.
successCriteria: Describe offline changes as local and unsynced.
Find both branches and compare attribution as well as amount.
Avoid assuming equal amounts resolve conflicting source attribution.
Review again if the heads change before committing.
observe: Whether participant labels offline state backed up
Local versus remote distinction
Response to review acknowledgement
Whether conflicting history is understood as preserved

tasks.prompt: Prepare a fictional encrypted backup and inspect how it would be restored on another device. The archive has no original source files. Also try the wrong-key or corrupt-archive outcome.
successCriteria: Explain that the prototype creates no real archive.
Explain why a real archive needs independently retained recovery material.
Find failed restore recovery without replacing an existing case.
Notice omitted originals and find source reattachment.
observe: Whether prepared simulation is mistaken for a downloaded file
Recovery material versus login-password understanding
Restore overwrite assumptions
Whether source missing state is expected after restore

tasks.prompt: You want to remove only one synced case while keeping the account and other cases. Try an offline request, a newer remote version, and a lost response. Then compare deleting the remaining device copy with deleting the whole account. Explain which copies remain and when completion is known.
scenarios: Stale remote head and renewed confirmation
successCriteria: Select one synced case without deleting the account, other cases, local copies or archives.
Explain that an offline request or stale-head refusal does not establish remote deletion and requires a current-head review.
Describe a lost response as unconfirmed, retry the saved request, and wait for a matching receipt before claiming success.
Explain that a tombstone blocks stale recreation of the deleted case ID while independent copies may remain.
Distinguish local case/key wrappers from server ciphertext, account envelopes and login identity.
Recognize pending/failed whole-account purge as incomplete and find retry and a signed-out safe exit.
observe: Scope words participant repeats
Whether local data or other cases are assumed erased by a single-case request
Whether a lost response is treated as success or proof of no deletion
Whether stale review requires renewed confirmation
Understanding of tombstones, surviving archives and account access
Whether login reset or logout is assumed to erase records
Response to pending and failure states

sessionTemplate.participantKind: human (must be verified at session time)

consent.scope: Non-sensitive task outcomes and written usability notes only
